      <description><p>President orders prompt investigation after one train derails in collision in al-Ayyat about 50km from Cairo</p><p>Seven people were killed and at least 125 injured when two trains collided on Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, officials said.</p><p>The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 50km (30 miles) south of Cairo, when a train travelling to Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the transport ministry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/08/egypt-two-trains-deadly-collision">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie</link>
      <description><p>Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families</p><p>The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.</p><p>The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children">found the cult leader guilty</a> of the crimes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/anc-faces-defeat-south-african-local-elections</link>
      <description><p>Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result</p><p>The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted.</p><p>Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994.       <description><p>Republicans pick Jordan as House leader and John Thune as Senate leader for last two years of Trump’s presidency</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/nov/10/donald-trump-pete-hegseth-thomas-massie-republicans-iran-war-impeachment-midterms-latest-news-updates">US politics – live updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Republicans have elected veteran congressman Jim Jordan as their new leader in the House of Representatives, putting a strident defender of Donald Trump at the helm of their conference as they navigate the fallout from sweeping losses in last week’s midterm elections.</p><p>Jordan will serve as minority leader under the new Congress that begins next year, where Democrats will have their largest margins in both the House and Senate in years.       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/10/emmanuel-brigitte-macron-defamation-lawsuit-candace-owens</link>
      <description><p>Legal battle escalates as far-right US podcaster continues to spread false claims that France’s first lady was born a man</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/emmanuel-macron">Emmanuel</a> and Brigitte Macron have brought a fresh defamation lawsuit against Candace Owens in her home state of Tennessee, in an escalation of a transatlantic legal battle as the far-right US podcaster continues to spread false claims that France’s first lady was born a man.</p><p>The Macrons first sued Owens and her media companies <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/jul/26/emmanuel-brigitte-macron-candace-owens-conspiracy-theory-jean-michel-trogneux">in July 2025 in Delaware</a> in response to what the French first couple called “verifiably false and devastating lies” being repeated by Owens on her podcast and on X. According to that lawsuit, those lies included that Brigitte Macron, 73, was born a man named Jean-Michel Trogneux – who is actually her older brother – and committed identity theft to hide a gender transition; that Emmanuel Macron was elected as French president as part of a CIA mind-control program; and that the couple are blood-related relatives committing incest.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/10/emmanuel-brigitte-macron-defamation-lawsuit-candace-owens">Continue reading...</a></description>
